articles.title: Communities restore mangrove forests that now protect coastal villages
articles.summary: Local volunteers and scientists have replanted mangroves along a vulnerable coastline, reducing flood risk while reviving fish habitats and livelihoods.
articles.body: A multi-year restoration project has brought mangrove forests back to stretches of coastline that were once barren. Villagers report fewer storm surges reaching homes, and fishing yields have begun to recover as nurseries for marine life return. The work pairs traditional knowledge with satellite monitoring so communities can track growth and protect young trees.
articles.explainability: Selected because it shows durable environmental restoration with clear human benefit, high credibility, and long-term community value. Editorial publication still requires human approval.
articles.imageAlt: Sunlit coastal waters with green shoreline vegetation

articles.title: Open workshop designs low-cost prosthetic hands for children
articles.summary: Engineers and clinicians released open designs for adjustable prosthetic hands, helping clinics produce fittings locally in days instead of months.
articles.body: A collaborative workshop published open hardware designs for child-sized prosthetic hands that can be printed and assembled in community clinics. Early pilots show faster fittings, lower costs, and easier adjustments as children grow. Training materials accompany the designs so local technicians can maintain devices without waiting for distant suppliers.
articles.explainability: Selected because it demonstrates technology with direct human benefit, strong accessibility impact, and practical deployment evidence.
articles.imageAlt: Hands working with tools at a maker bench

articles.title: City transit network completes fully accessible station upgrade
articles.summary: Elevators, tactile paths, and clear audio announcements now cover every station, making daily travel safer and more independent for disabled riders.
articles.body: After a decade of staged upgrades, a metropolitan transit authority reports that every station now meets full accessibility standards. The program added elevators, tactile guidance, boarding gap fixes, and multilingual audio cues. Advocacy groups that co-designed the plan say ridership among disabled passengers has risen and wait times for assistance have fallen.
articles.explainability: Selected for measurable accessibility gains that expand everyday independence and civic participation.
articles.imageAlt: Modern train at a bright station platform
